prompt: A two-sided one-sample $t$-test of a battery company's claimed mean lifetime gives $t = 2.45$ with df $= 24$. A $t$-table row for df $= 24$ shows that $t = 2.064$ has upper-tail area $0.025$ and $t = 2.492$ has upper-tail area $0.01$. Which range contains the $p$-value?
hint: Place $2.45$ between the two table values to trap the ONE-tail area. Then remember the test is two-sided.

hints.text: Place $2.45$ between the two table values to trap the ONE-tail area. Then remember the test is two-sided.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: if a one-sided test had $t = 2.45$, the upper-tail area would be between $0.01$ and $0.025$, since $2.064 < 2.45 < 2.492$. Now double it.
One tail: between $0.01$ and $0.025$. Two-sided $p$-value doubles both ends.

explanation: Since $2.064 < 2.45 < 2.492$, the area above $t = 2.45$ is between $0.01$ and $0.025$.
A two-sided alternative counts both tails, so double: between $0.02$ and $0.05$.
A gives the one-sided range — the classic slip. The answer is B. At $\alpha = 0.05$, reject $H_0$; at $\alpha = 0.01$, do not.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read the table as brackets
steps: Tables give a few landmark $t$ values per row; your statistic lands between two of them.
Bigger $t$ means smaller tail area, so $2.45$ (between the landmarks) has tail area between their areas: $0.01$ to $0.025$.
Two-sided: $0.02$ to $0.05$. A calculator would give $p \approx 0.022$, inside that range.
